soundness_flags.one_line: Theta_w(P) and Theta_+(P) are defined as feasibility fibers of F_w and F_s, so the theorem's displayed iff is presently a zero-step definition rather than the claimed equivalence to the legal feedback model.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies a binary panel with a predetermined binary covariate and unrestricted heterogeneity and feedback, characterizing its identified set with linear-programming computation.
The paper relates dynamic fixed-effects logit identification to truncated moment problems and gives finite conditional moment equalities with shape constraints and an SDP inference procedure.
The paper gives necessary and sufficient conditions for truncated Hamburger, Hausdorff, and Stieltjes moment problems.
The paper proves Tchakaloff-type finite cubature for Borel measures with moments through the prescribed order; the proposal's bibliography year should be corrected from 2002 to 2006.
The paper characterizes feedback-and-heterogeneity-robust moments and develops constructive moment-based estimation, rather than stating this positive sharp response-measure cone.
The paper develops identified-set estimators and confidence regions by inversion of sample criterion functions, with consistency and rate results.
The paper constructs computationally simple root-n outer bounds and asymptotically valid confidence intervals for average-effect identified sets, not exact sharp-set boundary inference.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define Theta_w and Theta_+ first as the model-generated legal-law/APE sets over M_w(c) and M_+(c), then state the finite-lift iff as their independent characterization; retain F only as the certificate.

Promote the response-measure reverse reconstruction and the open-half-line/common-support certificates into the theorem statement or a tightly referenced theorem chain, so the sharpness claim is visibly distinct from SDP feasibility by definition.

Add a constructive atom-extraction algorithm with a stated finite support bound and certified reconstruction of h and g; this would turn the exact cone from a representation result into a stronger practical partial-identification contribution.

recommended_next_step: Revise the circular definition of the sharp sets and restate the exact-cone theorem as an independent equivalence to the legal model, then rerun novelty review.
